daily_brief: The most consequential developments today center on escalating military conflicts across two theaters. The U.S.-Iran war has intensified dramatically after a month-long lull, with American strikes hitting Iranian coastal targets and allegedly killing civilians at a wedding, prompting Iranian retaliation against Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan [Globe and Mail, Al Jazeera, Financial Times]. Oil prices have surged to nearly $96 per barrel, raising inflation fears globally. In Europe, Germany has formally attributed last month's drone attack on Leipzig airport to Russia and announced the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, with the EU summoning Moscow's envoy and considering new sanctions [BBC, Le Monde]. Meanwhile, Ukraine's President Zelensky warned airlines to avoid Russian airspace as Kyiv escalates drone operations targeting Russian territory, with Putin calling the statement 'state terrorism' [BBC, Financial Times, France 24]. In Nepal, hope fades for nearly 4,000 missing as the death toll from catastrophic glacial floods surpasses 1,100, with the UN estimating 2.2 million tonnes of debris [RFI, Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to foreign collusion charges in a second national security case that could extend his imprisonment significantly [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia, France 24].

top_stories.headline: U.S.-Iran War Escalates: American Strikes Hit Iranian Coast, Tehran Retaliates Against Gulf States
bullets: U.S. Central Command struck dozens of military targets along Iran's southern coast, with Iran claiming a wedding party was hit near Kuhestak, killing at least four civilians including a child
Iran retaliated by firing ballistic missiles and drones at Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, and Iraq's Kurdish region; Bahrain intercepted incoming fire, while a drone sparked a blaze in Kuwait City
Oil prices surged to nearly $96 per barrel, up from under $90 last week, with European gas reaching a three-year high and bond markets reacting to inflation fears
President Trump warned Iran would be 'totally wiped out' if it continues to retaliate, while the renewed fighting ends more than a month of relative calm in the conflict

top_stories.headline: Germany Attributes Leipzig Airport Drone Attack to Russia, Closes Consulate and Expels Diplomats
bullets: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt confirmed Russia was responsible for the August 4 drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, where a drone carrying explosives was found near Ukrainian cargo planes
Germany announced closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn and termination of the Russian House contract in Berlin, while expelling additional diplomats
Putin denied involvement and accused Germany of planting evidence; the Russian embassy called the allegations 'absurd'
The EU summoned Russia's envoy and is considering new sanctions in response to what officials called part of a 'well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe'

top_stories.headline: Zelensky Warns Airlines to Avoid Russian Airspace as Ukraine Escalates Drone Campaign
bullets: Ukrainian President Zelensky warned airlines and insurers that Russian airspace is 'effectively closing' due to escalating Ukrainian drone operations targeting Russian territory
Zelensky stated Ukraine does not threaten civilian aircraft but warned 'there will simply be drones in Russia's skies on a scale that has to be taken into account'
Most Western airlines already avoid Russian airspace, but carriers from Turkey, China, and other countries continue to use it for flights to Moscow and St. Petersburg
Putin responded by calling Zelensky's statement a 'declaration of state terrorism' and vowed to continue intensified attacks on Ukraine

top_stories.headline: Nepal Flood Death Toll Exceeds 1,100 as Hope Fades for Nearly 4,000 Missing
bullets: At least 1,114 people confirmed dead in Nepal one week after a glacial collapse in the Himalayas unleashed catastrophic flash floods; China reports 16 dead and 546 missing in Tibet

Nearly 4,000 people remain unaccounted for, with officials saying hope of finding survivors is decreasing; rescue teams from India, China, and the U.S. are attempting to reach workers trapped in hydropower tunnels
The UN estimates the disaster left at least 2.2 million tonnes of debris; 11 hydropower stations and one solar plant have stopped operating
Nepal's foreign minister called the disaster 'a warning signal' about climate change risks, as authorities began burying unidentified bodies after DNA sampling due to overwhelmed morgues

top_stories.headline: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Pleads Guilty to Foreign Collusion in Second National Security Case
bullets: Joshua Wong, one of Hong Kong's most prominent democracy activists, pleaded guilty to 'conspiring to collude with foreign forces' in a second national security case

Wong was already serving a 56-month sentence after being convicted in 2024 for participating in an election primary deemed illegal; he was due for release early next year before new charges were filed
The charges relate to allegedly colluding with foreign forces to impose economic sanctions on Hong Kong, with most conduct occurring before the 2020 national security law was passed
Wong faces potential additional years in prison; co-defendant Nathan Law, who went into exile in 2020, faces similar charges
